name: Georgian porcelain tea service
summary: The first English porcelain tea services. A tea set of handleless bowls, a pot, jugs and slop bowls in soft-paste or bone china, with blue painting, enamel flowers and gilt rims.

philosophy.core_thesis: English potters make a full tea table in porcelain for the new tea drinkers: a set of matched pieces, with a Chinese or a European look.
design_principles: Make a set of 12 to 40 pieces in one body and one pattern.
Make the tea bowls handleless at first and add handles after about 1790.
Paint flowers, birds and Chinese figures in blue or in enamel colours.
Pick one border for the whole set: gilt line, blue band or scalloped edge.
Add gilding to the rim, the handle and the knob of the pot.
Make the pot rounded on a low foot, with a straight or curved spout and a knob lid.
Use the soft glassy glaze that pools in the corners and shows the tint of the body.
Copy Chinese and Meissen models first, and then design a new English form.
anti_patterns: A thick, heavy stoneware wall in a sandy colour
A single piece with no match in the set
A flat modern glaze with no gilding
A plain white pot with no border

form.shape: A tea service: teapot and stand, handleless tea bowls and saucers, a slop bowl, a milk jug, a sugar bowl with a lid and a bread plate. A caddy and a spoon tray may be added.
form.profile: A pot has a round or a barrel body with a curved spout and a loop handle. A tea bowl has a wide, shallow shape on a low foot; a saucer is deep.
form.foot_and_rim: A narrow foot ring on every piece; the rim is round or scalloped, with a thin line of gilding or blue.
form.proportion: A tea bowl is 7 to 9 cm wide and 4 to 5 cm high; the wall is 1.5 to 3 mm thick and the bowl is light.
rules: Match the shapes and the pattern across the set.
Keep the wall thin and the foot narrow.
Add one gilt line to each rim and handle.
Add a lid with a flower or a knob to every lidded piece.

bodies.rule: Use soft-paste porcelain in the early years, and bone china from 1748. Keep a stoneware body out: a thin, pale wall that shows light is the aim.

methods: slip casting of pots and jugs
luting handles and spouts with slip
painting in underglaze blue and in enamel
forming.joins: Spouts, handles and knobs are cast or pressed in moulds and fixed with slip; the lid is made with the pot to fit.
forming.details: Moulded leaf and flower shapes, a painted border, a gilt line, and a mark of the maker under the foot.

glaze.pattern: Chinese-style flowers and figures in blue; European sprays, birds and insects in enamel; borders in gold or in blue bands and scallops.
glaze.gloss: Soft gloss to gloss, about 70 to 95 GU; soft-paste glaze looks glassy and pools in the corners.
glaze.wear: Gilding rubs away first on rims and handles; the glaze shows fine crazing in old soft-paste pieces.

palette.strategy: A warm white ground, cobalt blue, and enamel colours in red, green, yellow and pink, framed by gold borders.

firing.kiln: A coal- or wood-fired bottle kiln for the biscuit and the glaze, and a small muffle kiln for the enamel and the gold.
processes: biscuit firing at about 1250 °C for bone china
gilding and a last firing at about 750 °C
firing.scale: Factories in London, Worcester and Staffordshire made services for the new class of tea drinkers, with 30 to 100 workers each.
firing.signs: A glaze with small black specks, a ring of glaze-free ground under the foot and a thin gilt edge.

pieces.form: Round pot with a curved spout and a flower knob, painted in blue
Handleless bowl with enamel flower sprays and a gilt rim
Helmet-shaped jug with a moulded leaf foot
Lidded bowl in bone china with a gilt line and a knob
Square tea caddy with a transfer-printed landscape

positive: soft-paste porcelain with a glassy glaze
handleless tea bowl and deep saucer
still-life museum photograph, soft north light

emotion.target_response: A polite pleasure. The viewer sees a matched service and thinks of the tea table of a well-run house.

use_cases: a period interior with a tea table
a set of matched porcelain for a product brief
a museum label for English porcelain
avoid_when: the brief needs a plain modern tea set
the brief needs hand-built tea ware
the brief needs a single heavy piece

modifiers.how: Cast the same forms in hard-paste porcelain and paint flat planes of colour.
Change the body to raku clay, remove the gilding and fire fast to 900 °C.
